features.title: Everything needed to plan safely
f1.d: Every opening half-day is simulated: a request that would leave the pharmacy without a pharmacist is flagged "not possible as is", with alternatives.
f2.d: Requests are ranked with a readable score (fairness, rotation, urgency, filing order). You see the rule applied and keep the final say.
f3.d: Occupancy rate, mid-year start, capped carry-over and Fribourg public holidays are handled automatically.
f4.d: The search ranks candidates by qualification, availability, daily rest and hours already worked. An apprentice is never proposed as a pharmacist.
f5.d: Quick declaration, instant alert, reminders, escalation, then a plan B (reduced hours or closure) with its impact shown.
f6.d: Family information is off by default, requires consent and is invisible to colleagues. It is never used to penalise anyone.
how.title: Three steps to get started
s1.d: Enter people, qualifications, schedules and your internal rules. No code required.
s2.d: Requests are sorted, coverage is simulated day by day and every proposed decision is justified.
s3.d: You approve, refuse or adjust with a reason. Knock-on impacts are shown, then the team is notified.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
q1.a: The product is designed around the Swiss nFADP: minimisation, role-based access, audit log. Sensitive data (family situation, health) is off by default and needs the administrator to enable it plus the person's consent. This prototype uses fictional data only.
q2.a: Rules from the Code of Obligations and the Labour Act (holidays, rest, Fribourg public holidays) are default parameters to be validated by a legal professional. They are not legal advice.
q3.q: Who decides, the tool or us?
q3.a: You do. The engine proposes a justified decision (rule, criterion, score). Every proposal can be changed, is logged with author and timestamp, and nobody approves their own request.
q4.q: Can an apprentice or intern replace a pharmacist?
q4.a: No. They count towards headcount but never as a qualified person, and supervision remains required. Each status has configurable limits.
q5.q: What happens with sickness on the same morning?
q5.a: The absence is recorded, an alert goes out, qualified replacements are ranked then contacted. Without an answer, it is chased, escalated to the manager then HR, with a quantified plan B.
q6.q: Can I try it without commitment?
q6.a: The no-credit-card trial is an example offer in this mock-up. Actual terms will be set before any commercial launch.
